title: Divergent Creativity in Humans and Large Language Models

paper.authors: Antoine Bellemare-Pepin, Francois Lespinasse, Philipp Thoelke, Yann Harel, Kory Mathewson, Jay A. Olson, Yoshua Bengio, Karim Jerbi
paper.venue: arXiv preprint (v1 2024-05-21; revised version adds Figure 2 with models released up to June 2025). Full-text PDF fetched and text-extracted; Tables 1 and S1 are images (read visually).

dependence.note: LLMs are benchmarked against 100,000 human Divergent Association Task (DAT) responses; every model score is the mean DAT of 500 independent chat-session generations. Per-response scores and words for all models are released (notebook/concatenated_results*.csv).

claim.statement: On the Divergent Association Task, 'GPT-4-turbo' (Table 1: gpt-4-0125-preview) scores markedly lower than its predecessor GPT-4 (gpt-4-0314) - mean DAT 75.96 (n = 500, SD 3.57) vs 83.99 (n = 503) - and below the human mean (81.04, n = 100,000), whereas GPT-4 significantly surpasses humans (Figure 1A-B; Figure S2: 0314 > 1106 > 0613 > turbo); GPT-4-turbo also shows the highest word repetition, with 'ocean' in > 90% of its word sets (Figure 1D).
claim.metric: DAT score (Olson et al. 2021): 100 x mean pairwise cosine distance between GloVe-840B-300d vectors of the first 7 valid nouns of a 10-word list; mean over 500 generations after excluding responses with < 10 valid words; prompt adherence = share of valid responses; two-sided independent t-tests between models/humans

original_values.note: Means/SDs recomputed by the card author from notebook/concatenated_results_2024-11-08.csv (Strategy = 'Original instructions', Temperature = 'Mid'); the paper reports them only graphically (Figure 1A, Figure S2).

claim.original_source: Figure 1 and Figure S2 of arXiv 2405.13012; per-response data in notebook/concatenated_results_2024-11-08.csv and notebook/total_responses_per_model.csv (GPT-4-turbo: 500)

messages.content: Please enter 10 words that are as different from each other as possible, in all meanings and uses of the words. Rules: Only single words in English. Only nouns (e.g., things, objects, concepts). No proper nouns (e.g., no specific people or places). No specialised vocabulary (e.g., no technical terms). Think of the words on your own (e.g., do not just look at objects in your surroundings).  Make a list of these 10 words, a single word in each entry of the list.
[control condition, separate sessions] Make a list of 10 words

params.temperature: default (1.0 = 'Mid'; 0.5 'Low' and 1.5 'High' only in the temperature analysis of GPT-4)

protocol.n_items: 1 prompt (DAT instructions) + 1 control prompt; 500 independent chat sessions each
protocol.evaluation: Automatic: parse the 10 words; scripts/dat.py (Olson's DAT; GloVe glove.840B.300d + words.txt dictionary; first 7 valid words); exclude incomplete responses; mean and 95% CI; independent t-tests vs humans and other models (notebook/dat_visualization.ipynb).
protocol.environment_check: Re-score the released GPT-4-turbo word lists (concatenated_results_2024-11-08.csv 'Words' column) with our DAT implementation + the same GloVe file: must give 75.96 before any new call.

budget.assumptions: sibling arm: the paper's own scheme is 500 independent generations per prompt at default temperature (no extra seeds needed): 500 DAT + 500 control calls; ~110 input tokens, ~40 output tokens. Adding the three strategy prompts would triple it.

judgment.rule: ANALYSIS_PLAN section 1 (sibling arm only, flagged): survival if the sibling's mean DAT (500 samples) is significantly below the archived gpt-4-0314 mean (83.99; t-test on archived vs new responses) AND below the human mean (81.04), with the gap of the same order (>= ~3 points); partial if below GPT-4-0314 but not significantly below humans; death if the sibling matches or exceeds GPT-4-0314 or humans (the 'newer turbo is less divergent' claim fails).
judgment.notes: The comparison uses the archived gpt-4-0314 responses (model dead) as a fixed reference; word-repetition ('ocean' share) is a secondary descriptive indicator.

domain_notes: The DAT is a validated, fast creativity proxy (semantic distance between nouns in a fixed GloVe space), so scores are bounded by the embedding and by word-frequency effects; LLM 'creativity' here is diversity of a 10-word list, not a judgment of quality. The paper's headline is that some LLMs beat the average human on the DAT while the top human decile beats every model; GPT-4-turbo's drop below GPT-4 is attributed to increased response redundancy. Default temperature (1.0) matters: GPT-4 at temperature 1.5 reached 85.6.
